name: Crabfolk
body:
Crabfolk are odd, alien-looking bipeds with a superficial resemblance to crabs.

Physical

While ordinary crabs have ten limbs, crabfolk have six—two legs and two sets of arms. The lower set of arms are fully articulated and end in claw-like hands capable of manipulating any kind of tool or weapon that a human could wield. The upper arms arch from the crabfolk’s shoulders and end in oversized crablike pincers, which are only capable of clumsily grasping, pulling, and lifting.

A crabfolk’s entire body is covered in a dense, chitinous plating. Its eyes extend from the top of its head, while a beak-like mouth is hidden behind a complex mandibles.

Crabfolk come in a variety of colors, and the males and females of different subspecies often display different coloration patterns.

Most crabfolk stand between 6 and 7 feet tall, but some continue to grow throughout their lives and can reach a height of 10 feet or more by the end of their lives.

Social

Crabfolk live in small tribal communities with simple hunter-gatherer cultures. They eat fish, mollusks, and aquatic plants, and make simple arts and crafts. They are generally nonaggressive and shy, but if pressed will do their best to defend themselves and the sea caves that they call home.

Alignment and Religion

Crabfolk are usually Neutral, seemingly concerning themselves only with the moment and not with issues of morality.

Rarely, one will develop resentment toward others and turn toward Evil—or conversely, a sense of compassion and turn toward Good.

Crabfolk spellcasters are usually adepts or druids. Their few clerics revere ancestral spirits and usually choose from the Healing, Luck, Protection, and Water domains, as well as the Ancestors [Repose], Flotsam, Oceans, and Rivers subdomains.

Names

Some typical crabfolk names include the following (choose or roll 1d12):

Banyabufai
Bennaebennuk
Hujayafang
Jatorok
Karangi
Kashamanuk
Kwalengai
Langamakung
Mwosolan
Ringabwani
Twonotai
Unyanmoshi
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are extremely tough, but you move slowly and lack personal presence. Your ability score modifiers are +4 Con, –2 Dex, –2 Cha [greater paragon]. (2)
Size Medium. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Monstrous Humanoid with the aquatic subtype. (3)
Speed Slow. Your base speed is 20 feet. Your speed is never reduced by armor or encumbrance. (–1)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Crabfolk. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Aklo, Aquan, Goblin, and Sylvan. (0)
Other Traits
Amphibious You can breathe both air and water. (2)
Bulky Because of your odd shape, you suffer an additional –2 armor check penalty whenever you wear armor of any kind. (–1)
Senses Darkvision. You have darkvision 60 feet. (—)
Eye Stalks Your eyes extend above your head on stalks and operate independently of each other, allowing you to see in all directions at once. You receive a +4 species bonus on Perception checks and are immune to flanking. (4)
Four-Armed You have four arms. The top pair end in large pincerlike claws. These claws can grasp and lift, but are not designed for fine motor control and cannot manipulate tools or weapons, holding shields, or making the somatic gestures of spells. The bottom pair of arms end in hands with opposable thumbs and are capable of any task a human hand would be capable of. (4)
Natural Armor Your hard carapace provides you with a +2 natural armor bonus to AC. (3)
Pincers You have oversized pincers at the ends of each of your two upper arms. These are secondary natural attacks, each of which deal 1d6 damage + 1/2 your Strength modifier. If you control a grapple, you can use your upper arms to maintain that grapple and still make attacks with your lower arms. (4)
Swim You have a swim speed of 20 feet and gain the +8 species bonus on Swim checks that having a swim speeds normally grants. (2)
Total: 22 RP (monstrous)
Alternate Traits
Camouflage You are adept at moving with great care so as not to be noticed. You gain a +2 species bonus to Stealth checks, which rises to +4 in aquatic and coastal terrain. This trait replaces eye stalks.
Limb Regeneration You can regrow severed limbs or eyestalks without the aid of magic. It takes 1d4 days to regrow any part of an arm or leg, plus however much time it takes for you to heal any Constitution damage and hit point damage. Severed eyestalks can be regrown in only 1 day. During this healing time, you must have complete bed rest and have adequate access to medical care, or else the regeneration time is doubled. You can regrow limbs lost by any means, including fire and acid. This trait replaces darkvision.
Scuttler You are adapted to land rather than aquatic environments. You lose the aquatic subtype. Your base movement rate is 30 feet, and you have a climb speed of 20 feet. This trait alters type and speed, and replaces amphibious and swim.
Soft Shell You come from a line of crabfolk that evolved without the thick outer shell that characterizes most of your kin, allowing you a greater range of motion. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Con, –2 Cha. This trait alters ability score modifiers and replaces bulky and natural armor.
Species Feats
Elder Crabfolk

You have continued to grow throughout your life, and now tower above your kin.

Prerequisites: crabfolk, age category old or older, character level 7th.

Benefit: Your size category increases one step from Medium to Large, with all of the benefits and drawbacks that size category imparts. You are between 8 and 10 feet tall, and weigh between 600 and 1,000 lbs. With this size increase, you gain a +2 bonus to Strength, but take a –2 penalty to Dexterity. Your reach remains 5 feet.

Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add a +1/2 bonus to your trap sense.
Druid Gains energy resistance 1 against acid, cold, or fire. Each time you select this reward, increase your resistance to one of these energy types by +1 (maximum 10 for any one type).
Ranger Add a +1/2 bonus on wild empathy checks to influence animals and magical beasts with the aquatic subtype.
